Recording rights
Rule 2 — United States public domain: Victor 88487 was commercially issued in the 1914–⁠1917 release group, before 1923. Documented

The publication range, not the 1914 session alone, supports eligibility. Commons marks this recording public domain. The unavailable upstream item supplies no inspectable licence; no claim of an upstream CC grant, exact publication day, or worldwide clearance is made.

Giacomo Puccini, Tosca: Vissi d’arte. Emmy Destinn, 23 April 1914; Victor 88487, C-14508-4. Digital transfer by Tim Ecker; slight restoration by Adam Cuerden, via Wikimedia Commons. Rights statement

  2. Internet Archive — linked Destinn transfer (not opened) — Not opened: item page returned 404; metadata endpoint could not retrieve item. No facts or numbers are taken from this unavailable page; transfer credit comes from Commons.. Accessed 2026-10-17.

  5. Opéra national de Paris — Tosca, 2025–⁠26 — Acts I–III synopses; Roman locations, painter and Attavanti, Scarpia’s coercion, letter before execution. Used for dramatic context, not timings.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Julian Morton Moses — American Celebrity Recordings 1900–⁠1925, UCSB Historical Discographies edition — Introduction explains that artist sections group records by release years, not session dates. Caruso: Victor Red Seal 1906–⁠1908 includes 89006 and 95200; 1909–⁠1911 includes 87043. Destinn: Victor Red Seal 1914–⁠1917 includes 88487. Opened as extracted text; not used to infer exact take or transfer pressing.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
